newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open flat to lower.

text.p: New York precious metals futures were called to open flat to lower Tuesday as London bullion was fixed at its lowest in more than three years.
COMEX February gold was called flat to $0.30 lower after trading in a range of $370.90 to $369.30 an ounce on ACCESS. February last traded on ACCESS at $370.50, off $0.40 from Monday's close.
In early bullion trade here, gold was quoted at $368.75/$369.05. London bullion fixed at $369.00.
COMEX March silver was called flat to 1.0 cent weaker.
Analysts in London overnight forecast further weakness for gold as a strong dollar against the German mark discouraged buyers, and selling by gold producers cast a bearish pall over the market.
COMEX gold stocks fell 27,116 ounces Monday to 1,103,716 ounces, while silver stocks rose 1,723,569 ounces to 148,451,569 ounces.
COMEX March silver last traded on ACCESS at $4.725 an ounce, off 1.7 cents from Monday's close.
NYMEX January platinum was called $0.50 to $1.00 weaker, with NYMEX March palladium called unchanged to off $0.50.
U.S. leading indicators for October are due at 0830 EST from Conference Board, with October's new home sales, forecast at 772,000 units, scheduled for release at 1000.
